scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold” (preprints/Graph-Decompositions-at-the-Integral-Expectation-Threshold-October-5-2026/graph-threshold-decompositions.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 175 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5c0b3a5fc1764ff3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist an absolute integer k ≥ 2 and an absolute constant L ≥ 1 such that, for every n ≥ 2 and every graph H on at most n vertices, the edges of H admit a partition E(H) = E(H1) ˙ ∪ · · · ˙ ∪ E(Hk) with pc(Hi; n) ≤ Lq(H; n) (1 ≤ i ≤ k). The pieces may be empty and may share vertices. The partition depends only on H, n and is fixed before the random host is sampled.
